---

**Natural bijection between one-dimensional subspaces of $V$ and closed points of $\mathbb{P}V$.**

Let $R = \operatorname{Sym}^{\bullet} V^{\vee}$, graded with $V^{\vee}$ in degree $1$, and let $R_+ = \bigoplus_{d\ge 1}\operatorname{Sym}^d V^{\vee}$ be the irrelevant ideal. Recall that the points of $\mathbb{P}V = \operatorname{Proj} R$ are the homogeneous prime ideals $\mathfrak p \subset R$ with $\mathfrak p \not\supseteq R_+$, and a point $\mathfrak p$ is **closed** iff it is maximal among homogeneous ideals not containing $R_+$. For such a closed point, the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p) = R_{(\mathfrak p)}$ (the degree-zero part of the localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$) is a finitely generated $k$-algebra that is a field; by Zariski's lemma it is a finite algebraic extension of $k$, hence $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=k$ since $k$ is algebraically closed.

---

**The map $L \mapsto \mathfrak p(L)$.** For a one-dimensional subspace $L \subseteq V$, define the homogeneous ideal
$$\mathfrak p(L) \;=\; \bigoplus_{d\ge 0}\,\{\,f\in \operatorname{Sym}^d V^{\vee} : f|_L = 0\,\}.$$
Equivalently, $\mathfrak p(L)$ is the ideal of all polynomial functions on $V$ that vanish on the line $L$.

*Homogeneous and prime.* The quotient $R/\mathfrak p(L) \cong \operatorname{Sym}^{\bullet}(L^{\vee}) \cong k[t]$ (with $\deg t = 1$) is a graded domain, so $\mathfrak p(L)$ is a homogeneous prime ideal.

*Does not contain $R_+$.* Since $L\neq 0$, there exists a linear form $\ell\in V^{\vee}$ with $\ell|_L\neq 0$, i.e. $\ell\notin\mathfrak p(L)_1$; hence $R_+\not\subseteq\mathfrak p(L)$.

*Maximality (closed point).* The homogeneous ideals of $k[t]$ are $(0)$ and $(t^n)$ for $n\ge 1$. The image of $R_+$ in $k[t]$ is $(t)$. Among homogeneous ideals of $k[t]$, the only one not containing $(t)$ is $(0)$. Therefore $\mathfrak p(L)$ is maximal among homogeneous ideals of $R$ not containing $R_+$, i.e. $\mathfrak p(L)$ is a closed point of $\mathbb{P}V$.

---

**The inverse map $\mathfrak p \mapsto L_{\mathfrak p}$.** Let $\mathfrak p$ be a closed point. Pick a linear form $\ell\in V^{\vee}\setminus\mathfrak p$ (which exists since $R_+\not\subseteq\mathfrak p$). Define a linear functional
$$\varphi_{\ell} : V^{\vee} \longrightarrow \kappa(\mathfrak p)=k,\qquad f\longmapsto \bigl[\,f/\ell\,\bigr],$$
where $[\cdot]$ denotes the class in the degree-zero local ring $R_{(\mathfrak p)}=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Since $V$ is finite-dimensional, $(V^{\vee})^{\vee}\cong V$, so $\varphi_{\ell}$ corresponds to a vector $v_{\mathfrak p}\in V$.

*Nonzero.* $\varphi_{\ell}(\ell)=[\ell/\ell]=1\neq 0$, so $v_{\mathfrak p}\neq 0$.

*Well-defined line.* If $\ell'\in V^{\vee}\setminus\mathfrak p$ is another choice, then $\varphi_{\ell'}(f)=[f/\ell']=[f/\ell]\cdot[\ell/\ell']=\varphi_{\ell}(f)\cdot[\ell/\ell']$, and $[\ell/\ell']\in\kappa(\mathfrak p)^{\times}=k^{\times}$. Thus $\varphi_{\ell'}$ is a nonzero scalar multiple of $\varphi_{\ell}$, so the line $L_{\mathfrak p}:=k\cdot v_{\mathfrak p}\subseteq V$ is independent of the choice of $\ell$.

---

**The two constructions are inverse.**

*$L\mapsto\mathfrak p(L)\mapsto L$.* Let $L=k\cdot v$ and choose $\ell$ with $\ell(v)\neq 0$. Under the isomorphism $R/\mathfrak p(L)\cong k[t]$ with $t=\ell|_L/\ell(v)$ (so $t(v)=1$), a linear form $f$ maps to $f(v)\,t$. Hence
$$[f/\ell]=\frac{f(v)\,t}{\ell(v)\,t}=\frac{f(v)}{\ell(v)}\in k=\kappa(\mathfrak p(L)).$$
So $\varphi_{\ell}(f)=f(v)/\ell(v)$, i.e. $v_{\mathfrak p(L)}=v$, and we recover $L$.

*$\mathfrak p\mapsto L_{\mathfrak p}\mapsto\mathfrak p$.* We first claim $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak p(L_{\mathfrak p})$. Let $f\in\mathfrak p$ be homogeneous of degree $d$. Then $f/\ell^d = 0$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ (since $f\in\mathfrak p$), so $\varphi_{\ell}$ extended to degree $d$ sends $f\mapsto 0$. Under the identification above this means $f(v_{\mathfrak p})=0$, hence $f|_{L_{\mathfrak p}}=0$, i.e. $f\in\mathfrak p(L_{\mathfrak p})$. Thus $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak p(L_{\mathfrak p})$. But both $\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak p(L_{\mathfrak p})$ are closed points — maximal among homogeneous ideals not containing $R_+$ — so the inclusion forces $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p(L_{\mathfrak p})$.

---

**Naturality.** The construction uses only $V$, $V^{\vee}$, evaluation of forms on vectors, and the Proj construction; no basis of $V$ is chosen. Concretely, for any linear isomorphism $g:V\to V'$ the diagram
$$\begin{CD}
\{\text{1-dim subspaces of }V\} @>>> \mathbb{P}V(k)\\
@VgVV @V\mathbb{P}gVV\\
\{\text{1-dim subspaces of }V'\} @>>> \mathbb{P}V'(k)
\end{CD}$$
commutes, since $\mathfrak p(gL)=(g^{\vee})^{-1}\mathfrak p(L)$ under the induced map on symmetric algebras. Hence the bijection is natural (functorial) in $V$.

---

We have exhibited, in a basis-free manner, mutually inverse maps
$$\{\text{1-dim subspaces of }V\}\;\longleftrightarrow\;\{\text{closed points of }\mathbb{P}V\},\qquad L\mapsto\mathfrak p(L),\quad \mathfrak p\mapsto k\cdot v_{\mathfrak p},$$
and verified naturality. This is the desired natural bijection.
